shadows.name: object-drop-shadow
shadows.purpose: The system's one real shadow — a CSS filter (not box-shadow) applied directly to the item photo so it traces the object's own silhouette, grounding it on the stage without a card.

shadows.name: price-grounding
shadows.purpose: Offset text-shadow under the price digits; grounding, not a glow.

motion.name: odo-roll

motion.name: gavel-strike
motion.purpose: The large (up to 220px) gavel's wind-up-and-strike over 0.6s; impact lands at ~55-68%, cueing sound/flash/a scale-and-glow pulse on the price numerals/confetti and the name-capture field.

narrative.overview:
Two rooms, one palette. The MC's admin screens (setup, summary) stay an ordinary dark-gold operator tool — buttons, list rows, forms — because that work is done alone, at a desk, before the room is watching. The live auction stage is a different room entirely: a rostrum the MC controls in total silence, no button anywhere on it, because the moment it is live, every click would be a click the room can see. The keyboard is the only instrument; the object and its number are the only thing on screen.

This is a hard reset of that one screen, not a polish pass — it replaces the previous "Gilded Gavel" world's framed coin-tile digits, portrait spotlight frame, and on-screen bid/SOLD buttons outright, built directly from the user's own pinned reference (a dark-luxury antiquities/jewelry auction app) and their explicit brief: no clickable control anywhere on the stage, arrow keys move and bid, Enter strikes.
keyCharacteristics: Two visitor modes sharing one palette: Operate (setup/summary) and Experience (the live stage, keyboard-only)
Warm near-black, never cool navy or pure #000
One accent metal (antique gold), now rendered flat — no per-digit frames, no boxed tiles
A geometric grotesk (Bahnschrift) carries every number and Latin label; Thai copy stays in the Sarabun-safe sans
The digit-roll price ticker survives the reset as the system's one continuous signature motion, restyled unframed
Sage green is confined to the admin screens' sold badge; the live stage marks a sale in champagne gold, so nothing but gold ever appears on the stage

rules.name: The One Green Rule
rules.body: Sage green exists in exactly one place: the admin screens' sold badge (Operate mode). It never appears on the live stage, never becomes a secondary accent, and never becomes a hover state; the stage's own sold confirmation uses champagne gold instead.

rules.name: The No-Glow Rule
rules.body: Gold never halos. Emphasis on the price comes from size and weight, plus a real offset-and-blur shadow, never a symmetric colored glow.

rules.name: The Split-Script Rule
rules.body: Bahnschrift sets everything Latin or numeral; the moment Thai text appears it drops to the Sarabun-safe stack. Neither font renders a script it wasn't chosen for.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: Exactly one thing casts a real shadow: the item photo itself, via a drop-shadow filter tracing its own silhouette. Corrected from an earlier draft that put this shadow on a bordered card behind the photo, which still read as a picture in a frame. Every other surface separates with a gold hairline border instead.

dos: Do keep the live stage free of every clickable control — no button, no icon toolbar, no modal with Cancel/Confirm.
Do keep gold as the only accent metal, in both rooms.
Do keep sage green confined to the admin screens' sold badge only; the live stage's sold moment stays in champagne gold.
Do set every number and Latin label in Bahnschrift; Thai text drops to the Sarabun-safe sans.
Do keep the item photo's own drop-shadow as the system's only shadow; never wrap it in a bordered or backgrounded card.
Do draw new icons as single-stroke inline SVG in the gold/ivory palette. Never substitute an emoji for interface chrome.
Do guard every live-stage keyboard action against pendingStrike, so a stray key during name-capture can't bid or navigate underneath it.
donts: Don't put a button, link, or clickable icon anywhere on the live stage.
Don't add a glow/halo around gold text or borders.
Don't use gradient text for the price or any other emphasis.
Don't reintroduce the coin-tile framed digit.
Don't put a border, background, or box-shadow behind the item photo — it floats directly on the stage, grounded only by its own drop-shadow.
Don't reintroduce cool navy or blue-black anywhere.
Don't give the setup/summary administrative screens the live stage's full-bleed, keyboard-only treatment.
